branch_sharing_hazard.what: The Codex Temporal Gravity lane is committing to campaign/glm52-generation-b, the SAME branch this campaign integrates into. Commits 30b9894d, 2463cbb2, e68fd32f and 63c7555b landed interleaved between this session's integration commits, touching crates/hawking-core/shaders/gravity_pq.metal, crates/hawking-core/examples/gravity_pq_autotune.rs and tools/condense/gravity_lab_lease.py.
branch_sharing_hazard.why_it_did_not_corrupt_anything: The lane ownership map assigns disjoint file sets. Every commit from this campaign was audited after the fact against the forbidden-path list and all eight are clean; no Temporal Gravity work was swept into them and none of this campaign's work landed in theirs.
branch_sharing_hazard.the_actual_hazard: `git add -A` on a shared branch can stage another agent's in-flight work into this campaign's commit. It was used once, for the Bridge integration, and that commit was verified clean before this was noticed. It is luck, not design.
branch_sharing_hazard.standing_rule_from_now_on: Stage explicit paths. Never `git add -A` on this branch while another lane holds it. Audit every commit against the forbidden-path list before writing it, not after.
branch_sharing_hazard.not_escalated_to_the_user_as_a_conflict: Because nothing was lost or corrupted and the file sets remain disjoint. Recorded so the next session does not rediscover it the hard way.
